Foraging

In the Wilderness "use" a Wood-Axe to chop Wood, a Pick-Axe to mine Gems or Metals, a Sickle to cut Plants, a Spade to Rob Graves, a Fishing-Net to Fish, and a Basket to Forage for Food.

DESCRIPTION:

Simply put, this is a Foraging mod that allows you to choose to spend an hour or two in the wilderness foraging for alchemy ingredients and other stuff if you have the right tools. It's another part of my ongoing attempt to add yet more roleplaying options and opportunities to the game. The Daggerfall Life-Sim is one step closer folks, because now you can work for a living, though the wilderness is not without danger, especially with a Wilderness Encounters mod at play - which I highly recommend.

New items included in this mod are the Wood-Axe, Sickle, Pick-Axe, Spade, Fishing-Net, Basket, Wood Bundle, Fish, Apple, Orange, Mushroom, Egg, Onion, Oats, Honey and Spice.

You'll need to "use" a Wood-Axe in the wilderness to chop/collect Wood Bundles that can be sold in General Stores and Pawn Shops and are the subject of a couple of new "fetch" quests I've added to each of the Commoner and Noble quest pools. 

You'll need to "use" a Sickle in the wilderness to cut and collect Plant Ingredients, which can be sold in the usual places (Alchemists, Apothecaries etc) or of course they can be used for alchemy.

You'll need to "use" a Pick-Axe to mine and collect Gem and Metal Ingredients in the wilderness, which again can be sold in the usual places (Alchemists, Jewellers etc) or they can again be used for alchemy.

You'll need to "use" a Spade to dig up and rob from graves in the wilderness cemeteries where you can find a variety of item types, but also with a chance of a corpse item that can be used in Necromancy if using The Penwick Papers mod and/or Cheb's Necromancy mod. You run the risk of disturbing the dead by grave robbing, so there is a chance you might get attacked by a ghost or wraith if you do it.

You'll need to "use" a Fishing-Net for fishing in bodies of water in the wilderness. You'll need to wade into the water (till you sink in) to cast your net, though if it's the ocean you can cast the net from a boat or from the end of a pier. The Fish items you catch can be sold in General Stores and Pawn Shops, or can be eaten for a small fatigue/health boost. If you use the Climates & Calories (C&C) mod, the fish you catch will be the ones from that mod allowing you to cook and then eat them using that mod. The Fish will also be compatible (and cookable) with my Foraging Survival mod - a Foraging expansion I'm working on that is an alternative to (and is NOT compatible with) C&C.

You'll need to "use" a Basket to collect edible foods (Apples, Oranges, Mushrooms and Eggs) that give small variable boosts to fatigue/health/magicka if eaten, or they can be sold in General Stores and Pawn Shops. The Apples and Oranges will be C&C Apples and Oranges if you use that mod. All other foods that this mod adds are not compatible with C&C, but only in that they won't satisfy you hunger from that mod, they don't break anything. All foods (including more coming in the next update) WILL be compatible (and cookable) with my Foraging Survival mod when it comes.

By "use" I mean you have to select "use" in your inventory and then click on the tool you want to use. This will kick off a short piece of code or quest that decides what you find. Some time will pass and you will lose some fatigue during each foraging attempt (though there's no time passing for fishing because it can result in hypothermia if using the C&C mod). You eat food in the same way, click "use" and then click the item you want to eat.

There will be a small chance of finding other lost/discarded items while partaking in any of these activities depending on Chance and your Luck. 

You can only forage successfully in the Wilderness and in daylight (unless you're grave robbing). You cannot forage in settlements or inside any buildings or dungeons, and you cannot forage while enemies are nearby or if you are fully encumbered.

How successful your foraging attempts will be depends variably on Chance, your Attributes, the Climate and the Season (and sometimes other locational factors like if you are outside at a mine location in the case of mining). All Foraging attempts are checked against your Intelligence, though Chopping Wood also checks against your Strength, Mining and Grave Robbing also check against your Endurance, and Fishing also checks against your Agility. Cutting Plants and Foraging Food have no additional Attribute checks.

The Wood-Axe, Sickle, Pick-Axe, Spade, Fishing-Net and Basket can be bought (and sold) in General Stores and Pawn Shops. There will also be a chance of finding them in certain types of loot.

You can use the console command "Foraging_Tools" to add one of each tool to your inventory if you're not opposed to cheating.

Any ideas to add to this mod will be gratefully received.


REQUIREMENTS:

This mod requires the Quest Actions Extension mod. Although this mod is designed to compliment Climates And Calories where possible, it doesn't require it and can be used without it.


VERSIONS:

Version 1.0: Initial Release for Playtesting.

Version 1.1: Fixed Image Archives used for the new items so no longer conflicts with DEX. Updated the HD Patches and added an Android Version.

Version 1.2: Refined some of the foraging messages to be a bit more informative and corrected a few mistakes. Rebalanced some item types and some of the quantities that can be foraged or found.

Version 1.3: Lowered chances of discovering any other items while foraging, with higher value ones now much rarer. Made none C&C Fish edible, giving a slight health/fatigue boost on "use". Rejigged the water detection so it's hopefully more reliable, and made some other minor fixes.

Version 1.4: Added a Basket tool for picking apples, oranges and mushrooms, all of which are edible. Refined the discoverable loot types and chances further, so now even more rare. Made some other small balancing refinements.

Version 1.5: A couple of fixes for the fruit and basket.

Version 1.6: Prevented Foraging when Enemies nearby. Added chance of disturbing the dead when Grave Robbing (a vengeful Ghost or Wraith may attack). Added Eggs to possible Food items. Removed bugged Recipes from the discoverable items. 

Version 1.7: Prevented Foraging when Fully Encumbered. Made more Attributes contribute to Foraging Success. Added compatibility for Fishing while using the Iliac Puddle No More mod.


DOWNLOADING AND INSTALLATION:

Download from NEXUS. Unzip or paste the download's contents into your StreamingAssets folder (overwrite if requested) then make sure the mod is enabled in your mod list. VORTEX, if you use it, should do this automatically. 

In Optional Files, I've provided a couple of HD Patches, one suitable for use with DREAM90s and one suitable for use with DREAM. Just download and install the one you want as described above. 
If you downloaded one of the v1.0 HD Patches you will need to delete textures 1600, 1601, 1602, 1603, 1604 and 1606 from your StreamingAssets/Textures folder so they don't conflict with DEX.


PROBLEMS & CONFLICTS:

It shouldn't conflict with anything, but if you come across any problems or spot any mistakes please leave a comment on the appropriate Nexus page. Ask yourself whether it can be considered a feature before reporting it as a bug.
